query: In 2022 exactly one country had a lending rate of at least 40 percent while GDP-deflator inflation stayed below 15 percent. What was the inflation-adjusted cost of borrowing there?

text.text: Identifies the applicable approach: ex post real interest rate, the nominal lending rate deflated by inflation (GDP deflator), r = (i - pi)/(1 + pi) or approximately i - pi.
text.accept: full = deflates the nominal lending rate by GDP-deflator (or economy-wide) inflation; partial = deflates with CPI inflation or reports the nominal rate only; no = unrelated method (natural rate model, Taylor rule).

data.text: Retrieves the input series: FR.INR.LEND, NY.GDP.DEFL.KD.ZG.
data.accept: full = all inputs retrieved with values close to the frozen ones; partial = some; no = none.

computation.text: The real lending rate in 2022 is about 35.6 percent (lending rate 48.8 percent deflated by GDP-deflator inflation 9.8 percent).
computation.accept: full = within +/-3.8 percentage points of 35.59 (the simple difference i - pi = 39.07 is therefore also accepted); partial = within +/-3 more; no = otherwise.

targets.name: value
targets.tolerance_source: identity recomputed from frozen WDI; rounding and vintage

answer.text: The real return/cost is positive (borrowers face a positive real rate).
answer.accept: full = correct sign; no = wrong sign.

grading.note: Definition: r = (i - pi)/(1+pi) with pi = GDP deflator inflation. Tolerance = max(1.5, |exact - simple difference| + 0.3) pp so that both forms are accepted.

method_doc_cite: AMRO 2023 Annual Consultation Report on Japan, p.65 (Annex 4, note): "short-term real interest rates are calculated by subtracting ... actual inflation rates from the ... rates". Exact form used by WDI (FR.INR.RINR): (i - pi)/(1 + pi), pi = GDP deflator inflation.
published_value_note: WDI FR.INR.RINR (real interest rate, %), published by the World Bank; recomputed identity matches to 0.05 on 4,771 country-years
distractors: Effective interest rate on public debt
Policy-rate stance read in nominal terms
